images.title: 5 more bottles every day
images.purpose: Shows the container problem as linear growth: 5 bottles added each day, giving 200 after 40 days.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. Three columns of containers side by side, each column one container taller than the one before, with the day-40 total on the right.
images.exact_structure: Three columns on one baseline. Column 1: 1 container; column 2: 2 containers stacked; column 3: 3 containers stacked. Each container is a teal (#0072B2) outlined box holding exactly 5 small amber (#E69F00) bottle shapes in a row. Under the columns: 'day 1', 'day 2', 'day 3'; above them: '5', '10', '15'. To the right, a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box with '5 × 40 = 200'. Exactly 6 containers, 30 bottles, 1 box.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Adding 5 each day is linear growth: 200 bottles after 40 days.
images.description: Shows the container problem as linear growth: 5 bottles added each day, giving 200 after 40 days.
images.context: 200 = 2 × 10². Contrast with the doubling of the paper folds.
images.teaching_notes: Compare with the pond, where the amount doubled each day.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the same 5 bottles added each day separates linear growth from doubling, which is the point of this practice.
